title: The 20 Percent Plan Is Gone. But That Alone Does Not Explain Price Moves
part1:
What is a little interesting here is that the day after a plan with a clear figure—20 percent—was proposed, the proposal itself took a different shape.

On July 13, Mr. Trump posted that the United States would seek a 20 percent reimbursement fee on all cargo passing through the Strait of Hormuz, to cover the cost of ensuring its safety. The next day, he posted that the plan would be replaced with trade and investment deals involving Gulf countries and the United States. He said the decision was based on “very productive talks” with Middle Eastern leaders.
part2:
But the movement in oil prices cannot be explained by the fee plan alone. On July 13, Brent futures rose $7.29 a barrel and settled at $83.30. Reports linked the rise to a naval blockade of Iran, which was expected to begin the next day, and to concerns about energy shipments through the strait. We cannot say that the 20 percent plan alone caused prices to rise.

After the replacement plan was announced, Brent futures briefly gave up some of their gains. But before long, they returned to a high level close to where they had been before the announcement. At the time the article was published, they were up about 2.6 percent, at more than $85 a barrel.
part3:
At this point, you may want to ask, “If the plan was withdrawn, why did prices bounce back?” But we cannot tell from this price movement alone what moved prices. Reports said that U.S. and Iranian attacks, the naval blockade, and concerns about tanker safety were continuing, but these facts do not tell us exactly how they affected the market.

What we can confirm is that the proposal was replaced the next day, and that prices briefly gave up some of their gains before returning to a high level. Political statements can quickly change shape. But it is hard to understand market movements based on that one statement alone. That is what makes this news a little striking.
in_one_line: Trump replaced his proposed 20 percent Hormuz shipping fee, but oil prices soon returned near earlier levels for unclear reasons.
